title: Universal Rule Schema 8.2.4
description: Machine-readable rule structure with dual identity, evaluation logic, and lineage tracking. Finding lifecycle states are documented in x-finding-fsm (informative; normative source: SPECIFICATION.md §3.1).
x-normative-status: All x-* keys in this schema are informative and non-normative. SPECIFICATION.md is the sole normative source.

x-cross-layer-binding.policy_runtime_prohibition: policy_doctrine.yaml MUST NOT be read at inspection, evaluation, or FSM runtime
x-cross-layer-binding.runtime_executable_source: SPECIFICATION.md resolve_conflict over schema/CG-IR fields only
x-cross-layer-binding.rule: SPECIFICATION.md is the normative source. Schema is a structural projection of spec invariants. Policy describes governance intent only.
x-cross-layer-binding.version_compatibility_math: A rule dataset with schema version S.S.S is compatible with policy version P.P.P if and only if major(S) == major(P). Formally: dataset(s) accepts policy(p) ⟺ ⌊s⌋ == ⌊p⌋. MINOR and PATCH differences are compatible within the same MAJOR family. A validator MUST reject datasets where major versions differ.
x-cross-layer-binding.cross_field_constraints: evaluator_type ↔ evaluator_config consistency is a semantic invariant. JSON Schema if/then is a first-pass filter only. The compilation engine MUST implement a formal AST-walking validator per SPECIFICATION.md §2.9 Discriminator Validation. Intermediate validators that only validate subschemas may miss invalid pairings. Compile-time validation MUST use the AST walker, not partial subschema validation alone.
x-cross-layer-binding.policy_contract_version_check: JSON Schema cannot enforce that policy_contract_version matches the paired policy_doctrine.yaml version. The compilation engine MUST reject datasets where major(policy_contract_version) != major(policy.version) at compile time.
x-cross-layer-binding.audit_corpus: Formal verification audits MUST include SPECIFICATION.md, rule_schema.json, policy_doctrine.yaml, User_Stories.md, and this Contracts Directory (README.md) as the complete normative corpus.

x-discriminator-note.primary_discriminator: evaluator_config oneOf branches with required fields and additionalProperties: false — this is the sole structural discriminator for evaluator type safety
x-discriminator-note.secondary_filter: allOf if/then not:{required:[field1,field2,...]} is a weak first-pass filter only; it rejects instances only when ALL listed forbidden fields are simultaneously present. Subsets (e.g. {pattern, field}) pass the not check but are rejected by oneOf.
x-discriminator-note.normative_gate: SPECIFICATION.md §2.9 AST-walking discriminator validator is mandatory; engines relying on JSON Schema alone are non-conformant

x-finding-fsm.note: FSM is enforced at runtime by the Finding FSM Engine, not by JSON Schema structural validation of rule datasets.

x-portability-note.schema_limitation: JSON Schema structural validation is necessary but insufficient for cross-runtime determinism
compile_time_engine_invariants: RE2-compatible regex patterns only — PCRE features (backreferences, atomic groups) rejected by RE2 linter pass
NFC string normalization enforced before evaluator invocation
IEEE 754 finite doubles only — NaN and ±Infinity rejected in numeric fields
UTC-only timestamps — ISO 8601 with Z suffix; ±HH:MM offsets rejected
x-portability-note.enforcement: Reference validator (§9.2.15) and RE2 canary vectors (§9.2.6) are mandatory compile-time gates; see User_Stories.md S-21, S-31

x-cg-ir-hashing.dual_hash_model: semantic_hash (evaluator, scope, depends_on, priority, conflict_resolution, status, created_at) + presentation_hash (description, directive_revision, control_version) compose node_hash per SPECIFICATION.md §2.6
x-cg-ir-hashing.edge_hash: SHA-256 of sorted {source: directive_id, target: directive_id}
x-cg-ir-hashing.snapshot_hash: SHA-256 of sorted node_hashes + sorted edge_hashes + provenance
x-cg-ir-hashing.incremental_reuse: unchanged node_body produces identical node_hash across snapshots

contract.policy_mapping: Machine ID in directive tables maps to rule.lineage_id (immutable root). Execution ID maps to rule.id.
contract.spec_mapping: node.lineage_id in CG-IR maps to rule.lineage_id; node.directive_id maps to rule.id

x-identity.pattern_relationship: Execution ID pattern extends lineage_id pattern by appending zero or more -SUFFIX segments. Base [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ is shared. On first creation, execution_id equals lineage_id (zero suffixes). After fork/merge/split, suffixes appended. Suffix segments are hierarchical history tokens encoding the operation chain that produced the execution ID (e.g. TRAF-001-A-B means fork then fork). Suffixes carry no independent semantic meaning beyond provenance. NOTE: The 'operation chain encoding' is a human-conventional interpretation — the regex pattern does not enforce any encoding scheme on suffix segments; it permits any alphanumeric tokens.

lifecycle.revision: Same lineage_id, same id, new revision. lineage field NOT required.
lifecycle.fork: Same lineage_id inherited, two new ids. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.merge: Merged lineage_id = lexicographic min of parent lineage_ids; new execution id per §2.2.2. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.split: Same lineage_id inherited, multiple new ids. lineage field REQUIRED.
lifecycle.rename: Same lineage_id, same id. lineage field NOT required.
lifecycle.retire: Same lineage_id, same id, status=deprecated. lineage field NOT required.

invariants.lineage_id_immutable: Once assigned, lineage_id is never reused.
invariants.uniqueness: lineage_id MUST be unique within a ruleset.

x-deterministic-serialization.number_encoding: integer as integer, float as IEEE 754 double
x-deterministic-serialization.nan_policy: NaN and Infinity are NOT permitted in serializable objects
x-deterministic-serialization.hash_algorithm_versioning: Version 1: flat node_body hash (deprecated 8.2.0). Version 2: dual-hash model (semantic_hash + presentation_hash). If hash algorithm changes (e.g. SHA-256 → BLAKE3), increment hash_algorithm_version. All node_hash and snapshot_hash values MUST be recomputed. Old versions remain valid for audit replay but new compilations MUST use current version.
x-deterministic-serialization.canonical_form: All objects serialized with sorted keys before hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.recursive_structures: For recursive evaluator_config: serialize sub_evaluators as array of canonical JSON objects. For lineage: serialize parent_*_ids as sorted arrays.
x-deterministic-serialization.schema_references: $ref resolved at schema validation time; not included in canonical form for hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.map_ordering: Objects with additionalProperties: keys sorted lexicographically before hashing
x-deterministic-serialization.normalization_rules: additionalProperties: true objects have keys sorted before hashing. Default values NOT injected into canonical form. Only explicit values participate in hashing.

inheritance.merge: Sorted-set union of all parent authored_by values

x-creator-provenance.enforcement: finding.waive denies if actor is in creator_provenance; finding.approve_remediation denies if actor submitted evidence

x-complexity-limits.not_chain_note: NOT composites (maxItems=1) may nest recursively up to max_composite_depth. Nested NOT chains (NOT(NOT(NOT(...))) are valid but semantically equivalent to a single NOT for odd depth or identity for even depth. Validators MAY warn on redundant NOT nesting.
x-complexity-limits.sub_evaluators_recursion: Composite sub_evaluators recurse via evaluator_config_entry oneOf union. Each nesting level counts toward max_composite_depth. The reference validator MUST walk the full sub_evaluator tree, not only the root evaluator_config.
x-complexity-limits.evaluator_node_counting: Each leaf evaluator_config_entry counts as 1 node. Composite evaluators count as 1 node plus the sum of their sub_evaluator nodes. Total across all rules in a dataset MUST NOT exceed max_evaluator_nodes_per_rule.

x-portable-validation.finite_numeric_required: All type:number fields MUST be finite (not NaN, not ±Infinity). Enforced at compile time by reference validator pre-pass, not JSON Schema alone.

x-conflict-resolution-binding.specificity_metric: SPECIFICATION.md §2.15 defines specificity as a composite score using scope_specificity_score from §2.8.2 and evaluator field binding. Two implementations MUST agree on specificity ranking for identical CG-IR node bodies.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.spec_model: Deterministic multi-factor: explicit override → compatible_overrides (symmetric pairs) → priority → specificity → recency
x-conflict-resolution-binding.schema_model: conflict_resolution field provides explicit override only; not a standalone algorithm
x-conflict-resolution-binding.precedence: Explicit override (conflict_resolution field) takes precedence over computed resolution. If no conflict_resolution field, spec multi-factor algorithm applies.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.cycle_handling: defer_to_cycle_detection via DFS (§2.15): any directed cycle in defer_to subgraph causes all defer_to overrides to be ignored; fall through to computed resolution. If target rule in defer_to does not exist or is ambiguous (post-fork), the override is ignored; fall through to computed resolution.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.compatible_overrides: Symmetric pairs {always_wins, never_wins} and identical defer_to targets resolve deterministically per §2.15 compatible_overrides(). Incompatible dual overrides escalate to Conflict Artifact.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.defer_to_resolution: SPECIFICATION.md §2.15 defer_to_reference_resolution (normative): resolve to active rule by execution ID; follow lineage chain for deprecated targets; if multiple active children exist post-fork, escalate to Conflict Artifact
x-conflict-resolution-binding.scope_boundary: Conflict resolution applies within same lineage. Cross-lineage conflicts are flagged as Conflict Artifacts for human review.
x-conflict-resolution-binding.policy_model: Declarative intent description only. Compilation engine implements via spec multi-factor algorithm.

version.description: Directive graph version (semantic version of this rule dataset). Distinct from cg_ir_snapshot_hash in SPECIFICATION.md §2.6. MUST share the same MAJOR version as the spec for compatibility.

policy_contract_version.description: Version of the paired policy_doctrine.yaml. Compile-time engine MUST verify major(policy_contract_version) == major(policy.version); JSON Schema cannot enforce cross-file version consistency.

policy_contract_id.description: Identifier of the paired policy contract.

metadata.description: Informational context only. MUST NOT contain executable hints. See SPECIFICATION.md §7.1.

upgrade_from.description: Previous dataset version this dataset was migrated from (e.g. '8.2.1').

upgrade_to.description: Target dataset version for next migration (e.g. '9.0.0').

migration_required.description: True if dataset requires manual migration steps before use with target version.

lineage_preservation.description: How lineage_ids are handled during migration.

merge_provenance.description: Explicit mapping of non-surviving parent lineage_ids during a merge operation. Mitigates lexicographic MIN provenance loss by documenting the semantic weight and context of each parent.

semantic_weight.description: Semantic importance of this parent in the merged rule.

context.description: Human-readable description of what the non-surviving parent contributed (e.g. 'payment processing rules', 'access control constraints').

merged_at.description: Timestamp of the merge operation. Optional for backward compatibility; strongly RECOMMENDED for audit trail completeness.

merge_notes.description: Additional context about the merge rationale.

rules.description: The list of directives. Every rule MUST have a unique lineage_id and id. Uniqueness enforced by external validator.

lineage_id.description: Immutable root identifier. Assigned once, never reused. Used for audit trail. Optional letter suffix for sub-rules (e.g. SC-115A).

id.description: Active execution identifier. May change on fork/merge/split. Used for CG-IR compilation.

type.description: Deontic classification: obligation (MUST), prohibition (MUST NOT), permission (MAY).

target.description: Who or what this rule applies to. Deprecated in favor of scope for structured applicability filtering.

scope.description: Structured applicability context. Replaces bare target string for deterministic scope filtering and specificity scoring per SPECIFICATION.md §2.8.2.

filters.description: Additional applicability filter predicates on target metadata or content.

field.description: Path within target metadata or content.

anchor_ref.description: Link back to policy document. section: refs or JSON Pointer per SPECIFICATION.md §7.2. JSON Pointer format follows RFC 6901.

evaluator_type.description: Evaluator type. Discriminator for evaluator_config. AST types are Selma-specific extensions for Python code analysis.

threshold.description: Finite IEEE 754 double. NaN and ±Infinity rejected at compile time per §9.2.15.

oneOf.description: AST walk evaluator config — walks AST tree counting matching nodes

root_node.description: AST node type to start walking from (e.g. FunctionDef, Module)

walk_nodes.description: AST node types to count during walk

oneOf.description: AST node match evaluator config — matches specific AST nodes with conditions

target_node.description: AST node type to match (e.g. FunctionDef, ExceptHandler, Call)

value.description: Value to compare against (string, number, list, object, or pattern)

oneOf.description: AST call check evaluator config — checks for forbidden or unsafe function calls

forbidden_functions.description: Function names that are forbidden (e.g. eval, exec, print)

target_methods.description: Methods to check arguments of (e.g. execute for SQL injection)

check_first_arg.description: Checks on first argument of target methods

oneOf.description: AST scope check evaluator config — checks variable usage patterns within function scope

root_node.description: AST node type to scope to (e.g. FunctionDef, Module)

variable.description: Variable name to track (e.g. b_continue, raise)

rules.description: Rules to check (e.g. must_exist, must_not_exist, first_value_is_true)

oneOf.description: AST module check evaluator config — checks module-level patterns
AST context check evaluator config — ensures resource functions are used with context managers

target_functions.description: Functions that must be used in context managers (e.g. open, Popen)

must_be_inside.description: Required enclosing AST node types (e.g. With)

or_try_finally.description: Whether try/finally is an acceptable alternative

directive_revision.description: Revision identifier of the source directive (e.g. 'v3', '2026-07-05-r2'). Maps to CG-IR node.directive_revision.

control_version.description: Version of evaluation logic for this rule. Maps to CG-IR node.control_version.

metadata.description: Per-rule metadata. Informational only — MUST NOT contain executable hints. See SPECIFICATION.md §7.1. metadata.audit.authored_by is required for active rules and compiled to creator_provenance per §3.2.

authored_by.description: Actor ID of directive creator. Inherited through lineage operations. Compiled to creator_provenance for segregation enforcement.

depends_on.description: IDs of rules that must be evaluated first.

conflicts_with.description: IDs of rules that cannot coexist.

conflict_resolution.description: Explicit conflict resolution override. Takes precedence over computed resolution per SPECIFICATION.md Section 2.15.

defer_to.description: Rule ID to defer to (required if strategy=defer_to)

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Participates in conflict resolution recency step (§2.15).

lineage.description: Tracks identity lifecycle operations. REQUIRED for fork, merge, split. NOT required for revision, rename, retire.

parent_lineage_ids.description: Immutable root IDs of parent directives. Cardinality: fork/split=1, merge=2.

parent_execution_ids.description: Active execution IDs of parent directives at time of operation. Cardinality matches parent_lineage_ids.

lineage_id.description: Immutable root identifier for individual rule objects.

id.description: Active execution identifier for individual rule objects.

evaluator_type.description: Evaluator type for individual rule objects.

evaluator_config.description: Evaluator configuration for individual rule objects.

utc_datetime.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (Z suffix required). Offsets (±HH:MM) are rejected per SPECIFICATION.md §9.2.15.

evaluator_config_entry.description: A single sub-evaluator entry within a composite evaluator. Strict recursive typed union.
